HISTORY AND PHYSICAL (H&P) NOTE

History:
• 4-day history of upper-respiratory symptoms beginning with painful sore throat (odynophagia for 1–2 days), followed by clear rhinorrhoea, nasal congestion, and onset of a persistent dry cough yesterday.  
• Initial low-grade fever responded to self-administered paracetamol and ibuprofen; afebrile since.  
• Associated symptoms: night sweats, generalized fatigue, intermittent diffuse headaches, recent myalgias, mild exertional shortness of breath; no dyspnoea at rest.  
• Denies chest pain, ear pain/discharge, visual changes, photophobia, nausea, vomiting, rash, bowel or urinary complaints.  
• Slightly reduced appetite; increased fluid intake.  
• Possible exposure: close colleague sneezing at work (likely viral contact).  
• No similar prior episodes reported.

Past Medical History:
• No chronic illnesses or prior hospitalizations reported.  
• Medications: Paracetamol (dose/route/frequency not documented) and Ibuprofen (dose/route/frequency not documented) as needed for fever/pain.  
• Drug allergies: None known.  
• Family history: Grandmother with type 2 diabetes; great-grandfather with eczema.  
• Social: Lives alone; accountant. Occasional cigar smoking at social events; minimal social alcohol. Reports work stress but mood good. No recreational drug use noted.

Physical Examination:
(Tele-consultation; no in-person exam)  
• General: Appears fatigued (based on history); otherwise findings not recorded.  
• HEENT, Neck, Chest/Lungs, Cardiovascular, Abdomen, Skin, Neurologic: Not recorded.  
• Vitals: Not recorded.

Impression:
Likely self-limited viral upper respiratory tract infection / early influenza-like illness.  
DDx aligned with history:  
1. Viral URI (common cold) – classic symptom progression; improvement already noted.  
2. Influenza – systemic symptoms and night sweats consistent, though fever brief.  
3. Mild COVID-19 – overlapping features; consider if epidemiologically relevant.

Management Plan:
• Supportive care: Rest, increased oral fluids, continue paracetamol and/or ibuprofen as needed.  
• Work: Advised 1–2 days off to recuperate.  
• Red-flag instructions: Seek urgent care if high or persistent fever, worsening cough or shortness of breath, chest pain, or no improvement within 7 days.  
• Follow-up: Return visit or phone review next week if symptoms persist or sooner for any deterioration.  
• No antibiotics prescribed; rationale explained (viral etiology suspected).  
• COVID-19 testing discussed if symptoms change or exposure confirmed (not mandated at this stage).

Patient Summary:
A previously healthy adult with a 4-day course of sore throat, congestion, and new dry cough—with night sweats and mild systemic symptoms—most consistent with a viral URI/early flu. Supportive care given; safety-net advice provided.

Key Takeaways:
• Rest, stay well-hydrated, and continue OTC paracetamol/ibuprofen for comfort.  
• Take at least two days off work to aid recovery.  
• Monitor for fever, breathing difficulty, or chest pain—seek medical attention promptly if these occur.

Next Steps:
• Re-evaluate in 7 days if not improving.  
• Consider COVID-19 or influenza testing if symptoms worsen or community prevalence high.  
• No routine labs or imaging unless clinical picture changes.
